title: Return statistics, indicator correlation and parameter sensitivity
summary: Describe a test by its whole spread of results, treat indicators built from the same prices as one input, and check that nearby settings give similar results.
unreliableWhen: With few trades, every statistic is very uncertain. Low parameter sensitivity does not prove an edge; it only shows the result does not hinge on one number.
goodExample: Reporting average +0.2R alongside a median of −1R, and noting that removing the best trade turns the total negative.
badExample: Counting RSI and MACD agreeing as two confirmations, or publishing the one average length that worked best.

chart.lookFor: Note the candles where RSI 14 turns. Switch the lower pane to MACD and check whether it turns at about the same places.
